meta.description: English-language flagship demo for Wikipedia/Wikimedia audiences: impact-primary consensus, Deccan contribution dispute, pre-impact dinosaur decline debate, and Wikipedia policy alignment.
meta.warning: This is a structured source-weighting demo, not a complete literature review or article draft.

wiki_pages.title: Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction overview
wiki_pages.scope: Flagship overview page connecting cause, mechanisms, controversy, and Wikipedia-facing source weighting.

wiki_pages.title: Chicxulub impact
wiki_pages.scope: Physical impact evidence and impact-primary interpretation.

wiki_pages.title: K–Pg boundary evidence
wiki_pages.scope: Iridium anomaly, ejecta-rich layer, shocked materials, and boundary stratigraphy.

wiki_pages.title: K–Pg chronology and dating
wiki_pages.scope: Timing evidence connecting impact, extinction onset, and Deccan eruptive phases.

wiki_pages.title: Deccan Traps volcanism
wiki_pages.scope: Volcanic timing, contribution hypotheses, and Deccan-only overclaim handling.

wiki_pages.title: Extinction climate mechanisms
wiki_pages.scope: Impact winter, habitat suitability, carbon cycle, and sulfur uncertainty.

wiki_pages.title: Dinosaur diversity before the impact
wiki_pages.scope: Pre-impact decline vs sudden extinction, regional persistence, and global caution.

wiki_pages.title: Fossil-record and sampling bias
wiki_pages.scope: Methodological limitations in dinosaur diversity estimates.

wiki_pages.title: Impact winter
wiki_pages.scope: Mechanism-level representation of dust, aerosols, soot, sunlight loss, cooling, and uncertainty.

wiki_pages.title: Wikipedia editorial policies
wiki_pages.scope: NPOV, verifiability, no original research, and product-positioning guardrails.

wiki_pages.title: Public simplifications
wiki_pages.scope: Common public shorthand kept separate from source-backed scientific claims.

claims.title: Chicxulub impact was the primary proximate cause
claims.desc: The source-weighted view is that the Chicxulub asteroid impact was the main immediate driver of the K–Pg mass extinction.
claims.fc: Would be weakened by high-resolution global evidence placing extinction onset outside impact timing or by a better-supported non-impact kill mechanism.

audit.note: Consensus-level claim, but still worded as primary proximate cause rather than sole cause.

claims.title: Global boundary ejecta / iridium layer supports an impact event
claims.desc: Iridium anomaly, ejecta, and boundary stratigraphy provide strong physical evidence for a globally consequential impact near the K–Pg boundary.
claims.fc: Would be weakened by showing the boundary signal is regional, diachronous, or non-impact in origin.

claims.title: Impact winter and food-web collapse are plausible kill mechanisms
claims.desc: Aerosols, dust, soot, cooling, darkness, acidification, and photosynthesis collapse form a plausible pathway from impact to extinction.
claims.fc: Would be weakened if physically realistic models failed to generate severe enough environmental disruption at the right duration.

claims.title: Deccan volcanism plausibly contributed background environmental stress
claims.desc: Deccan Traps eruptions overlap the broader K–Pg interval and may have contributed stress, climate perturbation, or recovery dynamics.
claims.fc: Would be strengthened by tighter causal links between eruptions, volatile release, biotic stress, and extinction timing; weakened if outgassing is shown too early/late or too small.

audit.note: Keep as contributor/background, not equal alternative to impact-primary unless sources justify it.

claims.title: Deccan volcanism alone is established as the main cause
claims.desc: A Deccan-only conclusion is not source-weighted as established in this demo.
claims.fc: Would require a high-resolution causal chain showing volcanic forcing alone matches extinction timing, severity, selectivity, and global markers better than impact models.

audit.note: Kept visible to show minority/overclaim handling.

claims.title: “Impact alone, no meaningful background stress” is too clean
claims.desc: Even majority-side shorthand can be overclean; Deccan timing and pre-impact ecological debate require caveats.
claims.fc: Would be strengthened if Deccan and pre-impact ecological signals are shown irrelevant to biotic stress and recovery.

audit.note: This prevents the graph from becoming a pro-consensus propaganda diagram.

claims.title: Impact may have affected Deccan eruptive tempo
claims.desc: Some timing models raise the possibility of interaction between the impact and Deccan magmatic system, but this is not a settled causal claim.
claims.fc: Would need convergent geochronology, petrology, and mechanistic modeling showing impact-triggered eruptive changes.

claims.title: Press-pulse framing: background stress plus abrupt impact pulse
claims.desc: A readable synthesis can treat Deccan or ecological stress as press/background and Chicxulub as the decisive pulse.
claims.fc: Would be weakened if background stress signals are not globally robust or if impact-only timing explains observed patterns without residuals.

claims.title: Non-avian dinosaurs were declining before the impact
claims.desc: Some diversity models infer decline before the impact, but the global scope and fossil-record bias remain disputed.
claims.fc: Would need globally representative, sampling-corrected fossil data showing consistent pre-impact decline across major lineages and regions.

claims.title: The final extinction was abrupt; global pre-impact decline is not established
claims.desc: Regional latest-Cretaceous faunas and sampling-bias issues caution against treating global pre-impact decline as settled.
claims.fc: Would be weakened by stronger global sampling-corrected datasets showing persistent decline independent of rock record and region.

claims.title: Dinosaur diversity claims must account for fossil-record sampling bias
claims.desc: Diversity curves depend on fossil preservation, outcrop availability, region, and statistical correction.
claims.fc: Would be weakened only if a particular claim used complete or bias-free sampling, which is unlikely for deep-time dinosaur diversity.

claims.title: Impact-winter sulfur magnitude remains parameter-sensitive
claims.desc: Uncertainty in sulfur/aerosol forcing should be separated from the broader impact-primary claim.
claims.fc: Would be resolved by stronger constraints on target-rock sulfur vaporization, aerosol residence time, and climate response.

claims.title: Wikipedia-facing view should weight claims by source prominence
claims.desc: The graph should show consensus and minority views with visibly different weights rather than flattening all claims.
claims.fc: Would fail if it were used to smuggle original synthesis into prose rather than visualize source-backed disputes.

claims.title: WikiGraph is an editorial aid, not a Wikipedia replacement
claims.desc: The safest positioning is as a dispute/source visualization tool that complements the normal editorial process.
claims.fc: Would be weakened if the tool bypassed consensus, obscured sources, or encouraged original research.

claims.title: Public shorthand: “the meteor killed the dinosaurs”
claims.desc: A useful public simplification, but it hides source weighting, mechanism uncertainty, and Deccan/pre-decline debates.
claims.fc: Should not be used as evidence; it can only summarize a carefully sourced article-level conclusion.

evidence.title: Iridium anomaly at the K–Pg boundary
evidence.source_summary: The foundational paper argued the boundary iridium signal was extraterrestrial in origin and predicted a globally distributed dust layer.
evidence.audit_notes: Strong geochemical evidence, but mechanism needs additional nodes.

evidence.title: Chicxulub impact structure on the Yucatán Peninsula
evidence.source_summary: Identification of a large buried impact structure linked to the K–Pg boundary.
evidence.audit_notes: Physical crater evidence strongly anchors the impact hypothesis.

evidence.title: Ejecta-rich boundary deposits and shocked materials
evidence.source_summary: Synthesis of global boundary evidence connecting ejecta deposits to the Chicxulub impact.
evidence.audit_notes: Review-level source is useful for Wikipedia article weighting.

evidence.title: Schulte et al. review supports Chicxulub impact as trigger
evidence.source_summary: Review weighs Chicxulub as the mass-extinction trigger while acknowledging Deccan timing.
evidence.audit_notes: High-value source for consensus weighting.

evidence.title: Carbon-cycle/paleotemperature modeling: only impact coincided with extinction
evidence.source_summary: Constrained timing of volcanogenic outgassing relative to impact and extinction.
evidence.audit_notes: Strong against simple Deccan-only framing, but modeling assumptions matter.

evidence.title: Habitat/climate model favors asteroid impact over volcanism for dinosaurs
evidence.source_summary: Dinosaur habitat suitability modeling supports impact-driven climatic effects over volcanism alone.
evidence.audit_notes: Useful direct dinosaur-focused modeling; not a final verdict by itself.

evidence.title: Deccan eruptions overlap the K–Pg interval
evidence.source_summary: Large Deccan eruptive pulses occurred around the end-Cretaceous interval.
evidence.audit_notes: Supports contribution/background, not sole cause.

evidence.title: U-Pb dating resolves Deccan eruptive pulses
evidence.source_summary: High-resolution U-Pb work provides timing structure for Deccan discussion.
evidence.audit_notes: Timing evidence is strong but causal interpretation remains contested.

evidence.title: Eruptive tempo of Deccan volcanism relative to K–Pg boundary
evidence.source_summary: Argon-based chronology informs pre/post-boundary eruptive tempo and possible interaction questions.
evidence.audit_notes: Strong chronology, bounded inference.

evidence.title: Model infers dinosaur diversity decline before impact
evidence.source_summary: Finds evidence of declining dinosaur diversity well before the impact for selected clades.
evidence.audit_notes: Should be linked to sampling-bias caveats, not used as settled global conclusion.

evidence.title: Condamine paper explicitly tests fossil sampling/preservation bias
evidence.source_summary: The same line of work acknowledges that fossil availability and preservation influence diversity estimates.
evidence.audit_notes: Prevents overreading decline models.

evidence.title: Recent work stresses geological sampling bias in decline/no-decline debate
evidence.source_summary: Recent methodological work is useful as a caution node before public release.
evidence.audit_notes: Exact bibliographic details should be verified before final publication.

evidence.title: Latest Cretaceous regional faunas persisted close to boundary
evidence.source_summary: Regional evidence of dinosaur persistence close to the boundary weakens broad global-decline overclaim.
evidence.audit_notes: Regional, not global, counterevidence.

evidence.title: Sulfur forcing estimates refine impact-winter magnitude
evidence.source_summary: Newer modeling/constraints adjust uncertainty in sulfur aerosol forcing.
evidence.audit_notes: Mechanism uncertainty should not be framed as impact rejection.

evidence.title: NPOV requires proportional treatment of significant views
evidence.source_summary: Wikipedia policy requires neutrality and appropriate weighting of views.
evidence.audit_notes: Policy source, not scientific evidence.

evidence.title: Verifiability requires source-backed content
evidence.source_summary: Claims shown in the graph must point back to reliable published sources.
evidence.audit_notes: Policy source, not scientific evidence.

evidence.title: No original research constrains graph-to-article use
evidence.source_summary: The graph cannot be used to create unsourced synthetic conclusions in article prose.
evidence.audit_notes: Policy source, not scientific evidence.

evidence.title: Public shorthand: “the meteor killed the dinosaurs”
evidence.source_summary: This is a popular simplification, not a distinct scientific evidence node.
evidence.audit_notes: Kept visible so weak/summary nodes are not confused with direct evidence.

evidence.title: Majority-side shorthand also gets corrected
evidence.source_summary: NPOV does not only constrain minority claims; it also constrains overclean majority-side simplifications.
evidence.audit_notes: Shows fairness of system design.

evidence.title: Review sources carry more article-weighting authority than isolated primary papers
evidence.source_summary: For article prose, high-quality reviews and source prominence should guide weight.
evidence.audit_notes: Policy/design guardrail.

sources.title: Extraterrestrial Cause for the Cretaceous-Tertiary Extinction
sources.notes: Foundational iridium-anomaly paper; powerful signal but not a complete mechanism by itself.

sources.title: Chicxulub Crater: A possible Cretaceous/Tertiary boundary impact crater on the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico
The Chicxulub Asteroid Impact and Mass Extinction at the Cretaceous-Paleogene Boundary
sources.notes: High-value review for article weighting; supports impact-primary interpretation.

sources.title: On impact and volcanism across the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary
sources.notes: Constrains volcanogenic outgassing timing and supports impact-primary causation.

sources.title: Asteroid impact, not volcanism, caused the end-Cretaceous dinosaur extinction
U-Pb constraints on pulsed eruption of the Deccan Traps across the end-Cretaceous mass extinction
sources.notes: Strong timing evidence; does not alone prove broad causality.

sources.title: The eruptive tempo of Deccan volcanism in relation to the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary
sources.notes: Strong timing evidence; supports Deccan contribution/interaction questions.

sources.title: Dinosaur biodiversity declined well before the asteroid impact, influenced by ecological and environmental pressures
sources.notes: Supports pre-impact decline; explicitly sensitive to fossil-record and sampling-bias issues.

sources.title: The structure of the end-Cretaceous dinosaur fossil record
sources.notes: Recent methodological caution on the structure and detectability of the end-Cretaceous dinosaur fossil record.

sources.title: Late-surviving New Mexican dinosaurs illuminate high end-Cretaceous diversity and provinciality
sources.notes: Regional latest-Cretaceous evidence; useful counterweight to global overclaims.

sources.title: Reduced contribution of sulfur to the mass extinction associated with the Chicxulub impact event
sources.notes: Refines sulfur/impact-winter magnitude; mechanism parameter uncertainty rather than impact rejection.

sources.title: Common public shorthand: “the meteor killed the dinosaurs”
sources.notes: Kept as a warning node: useful as public summary, not direct scientific evidence.

narratives.title: Consensus narrative: impact-primary
narratives.desc: Most reliable reviews and physical evidence support Chicxulub as the primary proximate driver.

narratives.title: Press-pulse narrative
narratives.desc: Impact as abrupt pulse; Deccan volcanism and possible ecological restructuring as background stresses.

narratives.title: Volcanism-only narrative
narratives.desc: Historically discussed but should not be presented as established in this demo.

narratives.title: Pre-decline vulnerability narrative
narratives.desc: Dinosaurs may have been ecologically vulnerable before the impact; active dispute.

narratives.title: Wikipedia editor view
narratives.desc: Represent major and minor views by source prominence; do not use graph as original research.

questions.title: What caused the K–Pg extinction?
questions.desc: How should impact, Deccan volcanism, and pre-impact ecology be weighted?

questions.title: Could Deccan volcanism alone explain the extinction?
questions.desc: What evidence would be needed to upgrade or reject a volcanic-only claim?

questions.title: Were non-avian dinosaurs declining globally before the impact?
questions.desc: Resolve global decline versus regional persistence under sampling bias.

questions.title: Which impact-winter components remain uncertain?
questions.desc: Separate impact-primary causation from uncertainty in sulfur, soot, dust, and climate parameters.

questions.title: How should this be presented to Wikipedia editors?
questions.desc: Show source weighting, minority views, counterevidence, and anti-NOR guardrails.

composition_maps.title: K–Pg extinction: cause overview
composition_maps.purpose: Flagship WikiGraph demo for a globally legible controversy: asteroid impact, Deccan volcanism, and dinosaur decline.

composition_maps.title: Impact vs Deccan volcanism
composition_maps.purpose: Shows why the impact-primary claim is stronger while preserving the Deccan contribution dispute.

composition_maps.title: Dinosaur decline before impact?
composition_maps.purpose: Displays the active dispute over whether dinosaurs were already declining before the final extinction pulse.

composition_maps.title: Wikipedia-facing source weighting demo
composition_maps.purpose: Pitch mode: demonstrates that WikiGraph complements, rather than replaces, Wikipedia’s editorial process.

tier_values.C: active hypothesis / weak or incomplete support

evaluation_model.m_tag_policy: M-only nodes represent public shorthand, analogy, narrative, or non-evidential material; they must not be merged with direct evidence.
